rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a lazy person.

example.english: Someone who never does anything and just lounges at home is a layabout.
example.traditional: 成日唔做嘢、淨係攤喺屋企嘅人，真係個懶人。
example.jyutping: seng4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5 zing6 hai6 taan1 hai2 uk1 kei2 ge3 jan4 zan1 hai6 go3 laan5 jan4

rows.note: Use this colloquial, mildly teasing term when calling someone lazy.

example.english: You refuse to get up and do your homework again—you’re such a layabout.
example.traditional: 你又唔肯起身做功課，真係懶鬼嚟㗎喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 jau6 m4 hang2 hei2 san1 zou6 gung1 fo3 zan1 hai6 laan5 gwai2 lai4 gaa3 wo3

rows.note: Use this colloquial and more strongly insulting term for a notably lazy person.

example.english: Everyone in the family goes to work, and you layabout stay home playing video games.
example.traditional: 屋企人個個返工，得你呢條懶蟲留喺屋企打機。
example.jyutping: uk1 kei2 jan4 go3 go3 faan1 gung1 dak1 nei5 ne1 tiu4 laan5 cung4 lau4 hai2 uk1 kei2 daa2 gei1
